why: Each interest label defines its own graph; 'shares the interest' means 'in the same connected component of that label's graph'. Run one union-find per distinct label, and every pair inside a component gets +1 for that label.
hints: Sharing is transitive per label, so for one fixed label the friends split into connected components. Edges with different labels never mix.
Group the edges by label. For each label, build a fresh union-find over the friends and union its edges; then every pair of friends with the same root shares that label.

Keep an n x n count table. For each label, add 1 to every pair inside each component of size 2 or more; finally scan all pairs for the largest count, breaking ties by the largest product i*j. That is at most 100 labels x 4,950 pairs, which is fast.
pitfalls: The same label may appear on several edges, even on the same pair. Group by label first so each label counts at most once per pair.
Pairs that share zero interests are still pairs, but at least one edge exists, so the best count is always at least 1.
Ties: among the pairs with the maximum count, return the largest product, not the first pair found.
Friends are numbered from 1, so size the parent array n+1.
